name: Mils bei Imst
kurzbeschreibung: Peaceful scattered settlement between Imst and the Fernpass – famous for its Baroque church and panoramic views.
text:
Overview

Mils bei Imst is situated in the Tyrolean Oberinntal on a sunny alluvial terrace at an altitude of 743 meters, approximately five kilometers west of the district capital Imst. With roughly 600 inhabitants, Mils is one of the smaller yet scenically most enchanting communities in the district. The village nestles against the sun-blessed southern slopes of the Lechtal Alps beneath the prominent Tschirgant massif and extends down to the banks of the Inn River. A regionally renowned ecological treasure is the Milser Au, designated as a Natura 2000 European protected conservation reserve and recognized as one of the best-preserved grey alder riparian forests in the entire Alpine space. Mils bei Imst combines tranquil village seclusion with close proximity to the outdoor adventures of the Imst region.

History

The fertile terrace of Mils, safe from river inundation, was already inhabited during the Bronze and Iron Ages, as confirmed by archaeological finds and historic field patterns. The earliest written mention appears in 1202 as 'Milser', an Alpine-Romanic toponym referring to stony ground or a mill site. For centuries, the community depended primarily on alpine agriculture, timber harvesting, and trade traffic along the historic highway through the upper Inn valley. In 1953, the village suffered a devastating fire that destroyed many historic wooden farmsteads; the subsequent reconstruction shaped the bright, open village layout seen today. The village's pride is the Baroque parish church of St. Sebastian, erected in the mid-18th century and adorned with exquisite Rococo altars and ceiling frescoes created by the famed Tyrolean church-painting Kirchebner family.

Getting There

Mils bei Imst enjoys superb transport links and is very easy to reach. By car, drivers take the A12 Inntal Autobahn to the Mils/Schönwies or Imst exits, continuing along the B171 Tiroler Straße directly into the municipality. Travelers arriving from Germany or Vorarlberg access Mils via the Fern Pass or Arlberg tunnel via Imst. Rail passengers travel via the Arlberg Railway line to Imst-Pitztal station or the neighboring Schönwies stop, from where frequent VVT regional bus services run directly to Mils. Cyclists touring the international Inn Cycle Path (Inn-Radweg) pass directly along the riverbank at the foot of the village.

Tips

An absolute highlight for nature enthusiasts is a walk through the Milser Au Natura 2000 European nature reserve. Along the Inn River, an informative nature trail winds through lush grey alder floodplains harboring rare wild orchids, dippers, and kingfishers. Another thrilling excursion is the trail through the Milser Schlucht gorge (Hallenbachtobel), where wooden walkways and a modern suspension bridge cross high above the cascading mountain torrent toward Gunglgrün and Imst. Food lovers and traveling families will enjoy the Trofana Tyrol adventure and dining complex, featuring regional Tyrolean cuisine, craft exhibitions, and an extensive playground. In winter, the nearby ski runs of Hoch-Imst and the Venet mountain offer relaxed winter fun.
